training-data.t: Eight toy customers: horizontal is **days since last activity**, vertical is whether they **churned** (red, top) or **stayed** (green, bottom). A tiny set lets us watch the whole training loop.

initial-parameters.t: With **w = 0 and b = 0** the model predicts **0.5 for everyone**, shown as the flat blue line. These parameters have not been learned yet, and the learning rate of 0.5 is **our** choice.

predictions.t: The dashed lines show the gap between each prediction and its true label. The churners (red) sit at 1 while the model says 0.5, so it is **far from correct** for them.

loss.t: The **loss** turns all those gaps into one number: **0.693**. A high loss means poor predictions, and training exists to make this number smaller.

gradient.t: The gradient shows how the loss changes as each parameter changes: **grad_w = −0.206** and **grad_b = 0.125**. We will move each parameter in the **opposite** direction of the loss rising.

update.t: Each parameter moves by **learning rate × gradient**, giving **w = 0.103 and b = −0.063**. The line tilts upward, and the loss drops to **0.667**.

repeat.t: The same four moves repeat: **predict, measure the loss, find the gradient, update**. Each faded line is an earlier version of the model. Every step uses the **training data only**.

loss-decreases.t: The chart shows the loss falling from **0.693 to 0.602** over five updates. A falling loss means the parameters fit the training data better after each step.

trained-model.t: The trained parameters are **w = 0.287 and b = −0.378**. **Remember:** training changes **parameters** to reduce the loss on **training data**. Judging it on new data is a separate job for validation.
